solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Agent that calms closers of serious crime case

indicators.note: a closer is what ends something, so the closers of two words are their last letters

parts.note: last letters of seriouS and crimE
the dative is a grammatical case

explanation.surface: A detective's sedative helps them unwind after wrapping up a serious crime case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' reads as a police investigation, but it is the grammatical kind: nominative, accusative, dative and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a calming drug is an agent whose whole job is to soothe.

clue.text: Perhaps David Lammy danced in Commons for Reform

indicators.note: the letters are offered up to be re-formed, rearranged into a new shape

parts.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

explanation.surface: A politician is imagined dancing in the House of Commons in support of the Reform party.
explanation.walkthrough: David Lammy became Deputy Prime Minister in 2025, so he is an example of a second-in-command; 'Perhaps' flags the example. 'Reform' borrows the name of the UK party Reform to hide the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: As Deputy Prime Minister, David Lammy is second in command to the Prime Minister.

clue.text: Head of demolitions returned explosive material

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
sent back, so the word runs from right to left

parts.note: first letter of Demolitions
a mine is an explosive device, turned round to ENIM

explanation.surface: A demolition boss comes back with explosives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosive material' reads as one phrase, but the split falls between them: 'material' is the definition, cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a hard-wearing cotton material, the stuff of jeans.

clue.text: Piece from Louvre in chiselled granite frame

indicators.note: only a small piece, the first letter, is taken from the word

parts.note: anagram fodder, rearranged to TRIANGE with the L set inside

indicators.note: granite that has been chiselled has been reshaped

parts.note: first letter of Louvre

explanation.surface: An artwork from the Louvre is displayed in a frame carved from granite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frame' looks like part of a picture frame at the Louvre; it is the definition. 'Piece' also tempts as the definition, since a triangle is a percussion instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangle is the frame used to rack up balls in pool or snooker.

clue.text: Bottles short serf brought up filled with Iodine

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its last letter
the reversed word has I put inside it
in a down entry, brought up means written bottom to top

parts.note: a serf is a slave; SLAVE cut short is SLAV, brought up to VALS
I is the chemical symbol for iodine, set inside the reversed serf

explanation.surface: Medicine bottles are filled with iodine by a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottles' looks like a verb but is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Vials are small bottles, usually for medicine.

clue.text: Small sounds of the enemy advancing for supplies

parts.note: S = small, as on clothing labels
time is 'the enemy'; as it advances a clock goes tick-tock

explanation.surface: Faint noises of an approaching army while troops wait for supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The enemy' is time, as in the phrase 'time is the enemy', so its sound as it moves on is the tock of a clock, not marching feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: goods held in reserve for later use.

clue.text: Boards son put down in Hackney home?

parts.note: a hackney is a horse, and a horse's home is a stable
s = son; the S at the top of the horse's home moves to the bottom

explanation.surface: Someone's son is put up for the night in a house in Hackney, east London.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney is a London borough, but a hackney is also a breed of horse, which lives in a stable.
explanation.definitionFit: A board is a table, as in 'bed and board' or a boardroom's table.

clue.text: He composed "Sweet Child" during lunchtime

parts.note: a cherub is a sweet, angelic child
in = during, as in 'in the night'
lunchtime is one o'clock, and one is I

explanation.surface: Someone wrote the song 'Sweet Child' over a lunch break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet Child' in quotes suggests the Guns N' Roses song; it is just a cherub. Luigi Cherubini was an Italian composer of operas and sacred music.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherubini was a composer, so 'He composed' describes him.

clue.text: Lead can?

definitions.meaning: a lead in an investigation, a clue that lets detectives proceed
the can is slang for the toilet, a seat one uses

explanation.walkthrough: The can is slang for the toilet, and the question mark admits the joke. 'Lead can' looks like a metal container.
explanation.definitionFit: A lead gives investigators something to go on; a toilet is something to go on in another sense.

clue.text: Uninspiring role featuring in performance

indicators.note: the role features inside the other word

parts.note: a deed is a performance, something performed
a part is a role in a play; it sits inside DEED

explanation.surface: A dull role in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uninspiring' looks like 'dull', but read it as un-in-spiring: no longer breathing in, so dead.
explanation.definitionFit: The departed are the dead, who no longer breathe in.

clue.text: Person who runs an addict about to get drug

indicators.note: the letters are turned about, rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, rearranged to CANDIDAT
E = ecstasy, the drug, added at the end

explanation.surface: A dealer hands drugs to an addict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person who runs' sounds like a drug runner in this surface; it is someone running for office.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Runs' is the election sense: someone standing for office.

clue.text: One scaled girder to secure rivets at the top

parts.note: a girder is a steel beam

indicators.note: only the top letter of the word is used

parts.note: first letter of Rivets, held inside the girder

explanation.surface: A steelworker climbs a girder to fix the rivets at its top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One scaled' reads as someone who climbed the girder; it means a creature with scales, a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish is covered in scales, so 'one scaled' describes it without naming it.

clue.text: European flower on display in Wayne Manor

indicators.note: the answer is openly shown inside the words that follow

parts.note: wayNE MANor

explanation.surface: A flower is shown in the grounds of Batman's mansion, Wayne Manor.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' is something that flows, a river. The Neman flows through Belarus and Lithuania into the Baltic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Neman is a river of eastern Europe.

clue.text: Room (executive) for a high-flyer's bodyguard?

parts.note: room = space, as in 'room to move'
suit is slang for a business executive

explanation.surface: An office is set aside for a VIP's security guard.
explanation.walkthrough: The high-flyer is an astronaut, not a business star, and the suit guards the body in a literal sense; the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacesuit protects an astronaut's body, so it is a bodyguard for someone who flies very high.

clue.text: Show about the Spanish is in poor taste

indicators.note: the word for show goes round, about, the other

parts.note: to indicate is to show
el is 'the' in Spanish, set inside the word for show

explanation.surface: A TV programme about Spaniards is judged tasteless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like a noun, a programme, but is the verb 'indicate'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: tactless, coarse, lacking refinement.

clue.text: Elated is how one could be after uninstalling Windows!

definitions.text: how one could be after uninstalling Windows!
definitions.meaning: windows are lights, so removing them leaves you without lights

explanation.surface: Someone is overjoyed to have got rid of Microsoft Windows from their computer.
explanation.walkthrough: Windows is the Microsoft software in the surface, but here windows are lights, and taking out lights de-lights.
explanation.definitionFit: Delighted means very pleased, elated.

clue.text: It taps in the morning around hill mostly close to Tulsa

indicators.note: the morning goes round the hill

parts.note: taps are marked C and H, cold and hot

indicators.note: most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a.m., before noon
a rise is a hill; minus its last letter RIS, inside A(RIS)M

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

parts.note: last letter of TulsA

explanation.surface: Someone tap-dances at dawn on a hill near Tulsa, Oklahoma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' looks like a pronoun starting a sentence; it is the definition, 'it' meaning personal magnetism, as in 'she's got it'.
explanation.definitionFit: 'It' is the elusive appeal someone has, which is charisma.

clue.text: National fruit

definitions.meaning: a citizen of New Zealand, by nickname
the fuzzy green Chinese gooseberry, renamed after New Zealand's national bird

explanation.surface: A country's national fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National' is a noun, a citizen of a country; Kiwi is the nickname for a New Zealander.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kiwi is a New Zealander, and a kiwi is a green fuzzy fruit.

clue.text: Huge moon sure to be seen in a different light

indicators.text: to be seen in a different light
indicators.note: the letters are to be viewed differently, rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

explanation.surface: A big moon certainly looks different in changing light.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about moonlight, which suits the rearranging instruction perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean very large indeed.

clue.text: What you'll hear announced in auction room

indicators.note: spoken out, so the answer sounds like the word

parts.words: What you'll hear announced in auction
parts.note: an auction is where things sell

explanation.surface: What an auctioneer calls out in the saleroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auction room' looks like one phrase, but 'room' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery.

clue.text: Old man moving in can and did upset German

indicators.note: the letters are knocked over and rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters
G = German, joins the fodder

explanation.surface: A father's awkward moves upset a German guest.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad dancing is the British term for the embarrassing dance moves of middle-aged fathers at parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Almost literal: a father, the old man, moving awkwardly on the dance floor.

clue.text: Chilled medium-sized chicken doesn't need starter

indicators.note: the word goes without its first letter

parts.note: M = medium, as on clothing labels
chicken = cowardly = YELLOW, minus its first letter

explanation.surface: A chilled mid-sized chicken can be cooked without a starter course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chilled' looks like refrigerated; it means relaxed. 'Chicken' is the adjective, cowardly, which is yellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilled, in slang, means relaxed, or mellow.

clue.text: Two thousand seats supply seating for attraction

indicators.note: the two Ms give the other letters a seat between them
read as 'supply' (in a supple way): the letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two thousand is MM
anagram of SEATING, sat between the two Ms

explanation.surface: A stadium with two thousand seats needs seating supplied to attract fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' reads as the verb 'provide', but is the adverb from supple, flexibly; that is what tells you to rearrange SEATING.
explanation.definitionFit: Attraction in both the physical pull of a magnet and the personal sense of allure.

clue.text: Maxim: married men should get a medal in the end

parts.note: m = married, as in genealogies
OR = other ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: only the end letter of the word is taken

parts.note: used as it stands
last letter of medaL
surface padding joining the pieces

explanation.surface: A saying that married men should be awarded a medal eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that surviving marriage deserves a medal; 'men' in crosswords is often OR, the other ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a short lesson or rule for living.

clue.text: Proportion of allowance patron finally cut

indicators.note: the last letter of the word
to cut something is to remove it, so the N is taken out

parts.note: a daily allowance of food
last letter of patroN, N, cut from the allowance

explanation.surface: A sponsor's share of the allowance is reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proportion of allowance' reads as one phrase, a share; the definition stops at 'Proportion'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses a proportion between two quantities.

clue.text: Flipping lucre and ultimately godless vices?

indicators.note: the word is flipped over, written backwards

parts.note: loot is slang for money, lucre; flipped to TOOL

indicators.note: the last letter of the word

parts.note: last letter of godlesS

explanation.surface: Money and godlessness as the root of all vice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vices' suggests sins, but a vice is a workshop clamp; the question mark admits the pun. 'Flipping' also works as a mild oath in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice is a clamping tool on a workbench, so vices are tools.

clue.text: Russian co-op using some cellular telephones

indicators.note: only some of the letters are used

parts.note: cellulAR TELephones

explanation.surface: A Russian collective relies on mobile phones.
explanation.walkthrough: An artel was a Russian workers' cooperative.
explanation.definitionFit: An artel is a Russian cooperative association of workers.

clue.text: He travelled in company car east of ruin

indicators.note: in an across entry, east is to the right, so the company car comes after

parts.note: to mar is to ruin or spoil
Co. = company
the Volkswagen Polo is a car

explanation.surface: A salesman drove a company car to the east, beyond some ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: Marco Polo was the Venetian merchant who travelled to China in the 13th century.
explanation.definitionFit: Marco Polo is famous as a traveller, so 'He travelled' describes him.

clue.text: Wife in party hooked up with fellow cheat

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: the party joins on in front

parts.note: a don is a university fellow
w = wife, inside: DO(W)N

explanation.surface: A wife got together with another man at a party, cheating on her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheat' reads as marital infidelity in the surface, but the definition means to swindle. To do someone down is to cheat or belittle them.
explanation.definitionFit: To do down means to cheat or get the better of someone.

clue.text: Conservative is defeated with popular approaches

parts.note: C = Conservative, the British party
loses = is defeated
in = fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: A Tory loses an election while a popular rival draws nearer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To close in is to approach, draw nearer.
